summary: The @gyomu/ts-analysis package provides a robust TypeScript static analysis and workspace discovery pipeline. It enables developers to initialize project contexts, analyze source files and package metadata, and manage filesystem caching and path resolution.
responsibilities: Orchestrate the static analysis pipeline for TypeScript source files and project configurations.
Manage project context, workspace discovery, and environment metadata.
Persist and load analysis results from storage to support caching and incremental workflows.
Provide path normalization, transformation, and mapping between source files and build outputs.

capabilities.name: TypeScript Static Analysis
capabilities.description: Inspects and processes TypeScript source files to extract semantic information, symbols, and code structures.

capabilities.name: Project and Workspace Discovery
capabilities.description: Locates and analyzes workspace projects, package configurations, and dependency catalogs to build a complete project environment view.

capabilities.name: Analysis Persistence
capabilities.description: Saves and retrieves file analysis results to and from disk for efficient caching and incremental operations.

capabilities.name: Path Resolution and Mapping
capabilities.description: Normalizes paths, translates between absolute and relative locations, and maps module specifiers and build outputs to source files.

designDecisions: Leverages external parsing libraries such as ts-morph to build comprehensive file and symbol analysis contexts.
Combines project metadata with filesystem persistence to allow cached and incremental analysis workflows.
Organizes shared infrastructure and domain logic into clear boundaries to separate path handling from analysis orchestration.
usageGuidance: Initialize the project context using workspace paths before executing any file-level analysis functions.
Utilize caching and persistence helpers to avoid redundant file analysis runs in large repositories.
Rely on the provided path transformation utilities to ensure consistent module and file resolution across builds.
